question: Every challenge so far passed against the fake model. What does that prove, and what does this module add?
options: It proves the feature gives good answers; this module only adds dashboards

It proves your code handles model behavior (errors, malformed output, tool calls); this module measures whether a real model with your prompt gives good answers on your users' inputs, and lets you see what each request did
It proves nothing; the fake model should be replaced by a real one in every test
It proves the model is calibrated
explanation: Handling and quality are different questions. The fake model grades engineering properties deterministically; evals and traces measure quality and behavior with real models.

question: Which layer does this module cover, and how does it relate to the others?
options: Layer 5, evaluation: it measures the decisions made in every other layer and produces the evidence governance relies on
Layer 1, model: it chooses the best model
Layer 3, harness: it adds permission rules
Layer 6, governance: it writes policies
explanation: Model choice, prompts, retrieval, agents and harness controls are hypotheses until evaluated. Governance (module 13) gates promotions on this evidence.

question: A team wants to replace its prompt and asks "is the new one better?". Which lesson builds the mechanism that answers it?
options: Lesson 06, tracing
Lesson 07, production feedback and drift
Lesson 04, regression gates: baseline and candidate on the same dataset, repeated runs, per-case diff and blocking rules
Lesson 03, LLM as judge, alone
explanation: A judge or scorer measures one version; the gate compares two versions fairly and decides, accounting for noise and critical cases.

question: An agent's final answers look right, but support finds it occasionally tries to delete accounts. Which lessons address this?
options: Lesson 02 only: add more exact-match cases
Lesson 03 only: ask a judge about tone
None: the harness already blocks it
Lesson 05 (trajectory evals flag forbidden calls, even blocked ones) and lesson 06 (traces show each tool call in production)
explanation: Outcome scorers miss what happened on the way. Trajectories in tests and traces in production make the attempted calls visible.

question: What does the ADR at the end of the module ask you to produce?
options: A ranking of eval platforms

An eval plan for an agentic reply assistant: critical cases, scorers, a calibrated judge, a gate within noise, product rule and CI budget, content-free tracing, review sampling and drift alerts, checked against a briefing
A benchmark score for the assistant
A copy of the tracing challenge
explanation: Like every module, it ends with a decision record whose plan is tested for coherence with the briefing's numbers.
